newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: Congo factions sign ceasefire agreement - UN envoy.
newsitem.headline: Congo factions sign ceasefire agreement - UN envoy.

text.p: the Congo Republic capital, Brazzaville, have signed a ceasefire agreement which should come into effect at midnight on Monday, the U.N envoy mediating in the crisis said on Saturday.

"I have been told by both sides that they have signed the document," U.N envoy, Mohamed Sahnoun told Reuters by telephone from Gabon. "I am always very sceptical but I think this will lead to a serious outcome."
Forces supporting President Pascal Lissouba and the militia of former military ruler Denis Sassou Nguesso have battled in Brazzaville for more than a month. Hundreds of people have died.
A ceasefire accord has been held up by Lissouba's refusal to sign it and Sassou's insistence that the president, not the prime minister, should endorse it.
Sassou's spokesman Francoi Iboovi confirmed the accord had been signed.

"The ceasefire has been signed. But in the meantime if we are attacked we will of course respond," Iboovi said. "If the ceasefire holds it is planned that it will be followed by serious negotations," he added.
